simple.meaning: עֲזָרָה (ʻăzârâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “an inclosure ; also a border.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 2 Chronicles 4:9. The surrounding context includes offering, altar, blood, priesthood, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עֲזָרָה (H5835) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: עֲזָרָה (ʻăzârâh) / H5835 is traced through 2 Chronicles 4:9, 2 Chronicles 6:13, Ezekiel 43:14, Ezekiel 43:17 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H5835. azarah עֲזָרָה noun feminine apparently enclosure ; — absolute ׳ע : 1 ledge surrounding Ezekiel's altar; הַתַּחְתּוֺנָה ׳הָע = ׳הָע הַקְטַנָּה Ezek 43:14 , below ׳הָע הַגְּדוֺלָה 43:14 ; ׳הָע alone 43:17 ; 43:20 ; 45:19 (see Commentaries). 2 outer court of temple, ׳הָע הַגְּדֹלָה 2Chr 4:9 ; with doors 4:9 ; 6:13 (see 1 חָצֵר 3. b , and on ׳ע in Herod's temple Now Archaeology ii. 78 f f. ). עַזָּתִי see below עַזָּה .
definitions.rootNote: from 5826 in its original meaning of surrounding;

occurrences.englishText: Furthermore he made the court of the priests, the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with bronze.
Furthermore he made the court of the priests, the great court, and doors for the court, and overlaid their doors with bronze.

(for Solomon had made a bronze platform, five cubits* A cubit is the length from the tip of the middle finger to the elbow on a man’s arm, or about 18 inches or 46 centimeters. long, and five cubits wide, and three cubits high, and had set it in the middle of the court; and he stood on it, and knelt down on his knees before all the assembly of Israel, and spread out his hands toward heaven)
From the bottom on the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the width one cubit; and from the lesser ledge to the greater ledge shall be four cubits, and the width a cubit.
From the bottom on the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the width one cubit; and from the lesser ledge to the greater ledge shall be four cubits, and the width a cubit.
From the bottom on the ground to the lower ledge shall be two cubits, and the width one cubit; and from the lesser ledge to the greater ledge shall be four cubits, and the width a cubit.

The ledge shall be fourteen cubits long by fourteen wide in its four sides; and the border about it shall be half a cubit; and its bottom shall be a cubit around; and its steps shall look toward the east.”
You shall take of its blood, and put it on its four horns, and on the four corners of the ledge, and on the border all around. You shall cleanse it and make atonement for it that way.
The priest shall take of the blood of the sin offering, and put it on the door posts of the house, and on the four corners of the ledge of the altar, and on the posts of the gate of the inner court.
